## Redo causes and termination status: what the log says about a rejected step and the end of a run (`apply_redo`) {#sec-ch13-redo-view}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Prints, for every rejected step, a list of the causes that rejected it. At the end of the run
it prints why the run stopped, and returns exit status 1 when none of the normal stop reasons holds.
**Switch.** None.
**Order.** Not a discretisation.
**Defining equation.** None; the section reads the decision of @sec-ch07-redo as a log.
:::

The mechanics of step acceptance (the six causes, the collective decision, the halving and the restore)
are @sec-ch07-redo. This section is the reader's side: what a line of the log means, and how to read the end of a
run.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the section states how the log encodes the decision. A rejected step prints
`Redoing the step with smaller dt (causes: ...)`. The list names each set bit of the globally reduced cause mask
once, in bit order: `floor` (1), `clamp` (2), `limiter` (4), `nan` (8), `saturation` (16), `vic-solve` (32). The 63
nonzero masks print 63 different lists, and each list decodes back to its mask; mask 37 prints
`floor limiter vic-solve` [check `src/snapy_report/ch13/redo_view_check.py`, output `redo_view_check.out`, `[C1]`].
When the redo count passes `max_redo`, the run ends with "Maximum number of redo attempts exceeded. Terminating."
If `vic-solve` is among the causes, the message adds "after restoring the rejected VIC step input" (`[C2]`).

At the end, `finalize` prints the first reason that holds, in this order: a terminate signal, an interrupt, the
wall-time alarm, the cycle limit `nlim` (when it is not negative) and the time limit `tlim`. If none holds it
prints "Terminating abnormally" and returns 1. Of the 32 combinations of the five reasons, only the empty one
returns 1 (`[C3]`).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch13-redo-view for the cause bits.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-redo-view
#| fig-cap: "The six redo causes as the log prints them: the bit of the cause mask, the word in the cause list, and the local test that sets it on any rank before the MAX reduction. A VIC solve failure (vermillion) is the one cause that still restores the step input after max_redo. The grey line is the message for mask 37."
#| fig-alt: "A six-row table of cause bits 1 to 32, their printed names and the condition behind each, above an example log line."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch13.fig_redo_view import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Each rank sets its six flags in `local_redo_flags` ([`meshblock.cpp:1278-1286`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1278-L1286)). They are reduced with
MAX and packed into the mask by `reduce_redo_flags` ([`meshblock.cpp:1288-1300`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1288-L1300)). `apply_redo` prints the
cause list and the two terminal messages ([`meshblock.cpp:1229-1276`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1229-L1276)). A Mesh with several local blocks
ORs their flags first, through `local_redo_flags` ([`mesh.cpp:431-437`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L431-L437)). `finalize` writes the final
output, prints the stop reason with the final `time`, `cycle`, `tlim` and `nlim`, and returns the status
([`meshblock.cpp:1121-1144`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1121-L1144)). The example driver returns that status from `main` as `status`, so a shell
or a test harness sees it as the exit code ([`run_hydro.cpp:202-205`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L202-L205)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The log names the causes but not the cells or the rank that raised them; the MAX reduction keeps only whether
any rank did. Only a VIC refusal prints its column, rank, step, stage and retry (@sec-ch07-vic-reject).
:::

1. **No count.** No meter counts the redos of a run; the count is the number of "Redoing" lines in the log.
2. **Single-block signals.** Only the Mesh path checks signals before the redo decision (@sec-ch07-redo).
